name: gizza-ai/csv-pii-redactor
summary: Mask, salted-hash, or redact chosen CSV columns

tool.description: Redact personally-identifiable data in the columns you choose of a CSV. Name columns by header (header=true) or 1-based index; the mode is 'mask' (replace characters with mask_char, keeping the last keep_last visible), 'hash' (salted SHA-256 hex code, deterministic so equal values map to equal codes), or 'redact' (replace with a fixed label). Non-selected columns and the header row are unchanged. delimiter is a single char or comma/tab/semicolon/pipe. Runs locally.

columns.description: Comma-separated columns to redact: column names (when header=true) or 1-based indices, e.g. 'email,phone' or '2,4'. Only these columns are changed; others pass through.

delimiter.description: Field separator: a single char or 'comma'/'tab'/'semicolon'/'pipe'. Default ','.

hash_length.description: hash mode: how many hex characters of the SHA-256 code to keep, 4–64 (8 ≈ short code, 64 = full digest). Default 8.

header.description: Treat the first row as a header so columns can be named and the header row is left unchanged (default true). With false, address columns by 1-based index.

keep_last.description: mask mode: leave the last N characters of each value visible, masking the rest (e.g. 4 → ****1234). Default 0 (mask everything).

label.description: redact mode: the fixed string every selected cell becomes. Default '[REDACTED]'.

mask_char.description: mask mode: the character each hidden character becomes (single char). Default '*'.

mode.description: How to replace each selected cell: 'mask' = characters → mask_char (length kept, last keep_last visible); 'hash' = salted SHA-256 hex code (deterministic, joinable); 'redact' = the fixed label. Default 'mask'.

salt.description: hash mode: salt prepended before hashing so codes aren't reversible via rainbow tables; the same salt+value always yields the same code (values stay joinable across files). Default empty.
